skill.name: developer-tutorial
skill.description: Write or audit developer tutorials with one new concept per step, resumable checkpoints, and progressively reduced guidance. Plan learner verification and troubleshooting around a demonstrable skill.
skill.summary: Create developer tutorials that build independent skills through focused steps, verifiable checkpoints, and learner testing.

content.user_title: Create Developer Tutorials That Build Independent Skills
content.value_statement: Developers can finish a walkthrough without learning how to repeat the task independently. This skill structures tutorials around demonstrable objectives, progressive exercises, resumable checkpoints, and learner verification.
actual_capabilities: Define demonstrable learning objectives, audience levels, prerequisites, and a single supported environment.
Draft tutorial pages with focused steps, expected outputs, troubleshooting links, and resumable checkpoints.
Sequence concepts by dependency and reduce supplied code as learners gain independence.
Produce prioritized audit tables from learner observations using defect, hidden prerequisite, concept gap, and friction categories.
Plan independent learner runs, transfer tests, checkpoint CI checks, and completion measurements.
Distinguish published tutorial guidelines from adjustable defaults for checkpoint spacing, guidance stages, and verification criteria.
limitations: Verified expected outputs require access to the target environment; otherwise the skill must identify unverified blocks and provide a run list.
Tutorial audits require observed learner runs; reading alone cannot establish where learners abandon or struggle.
The package supplies guidance, templates, examples, and evaluations, not a runnable tutorial application or automated learner-testing service.
Quickstarts, branching how-to guides, API references, video scripts, and curriculum strategy belong to other workflows.

use_cases.title: Draft an SDK teaching tutorial
use_cases.description: Build a focused tutorial that teaches one SDK capability through a working artifact, progressive exercises, and observable checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Repair a tutorial with high abandonment
use_cases.description: Turn learner-run observations into a prioritized defect table and rewrite the steps that block completion or independent practice.

use_cases.title: Create internal tool onboarding
use_cases.description: Design a hands-on guide with explicit access prerequisites, reviewer-visible checkpoints, and an independent final task.

prompt_templates.title: Start a tutorial plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a tutorial for [product] that teaches [capability]. Ask one question at a time to establish the objective and audience level.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish the learning goal before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a focused teaching page
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a tutorial for [audience] to build [artifact] using [environment and versions]. Include prerequisites, progressive exercises, resumable checkpoints, and troubleshooting. Mark every unverified output.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn a defined objective into a complete draft.

prompt_templates.title: Audit observed learner problems
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [tutorial] using these learner-run notes: [observations]. Return a step-keyed table of problems, event categories, and fixes. Prioritize by learners blocked and rewrite failing steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: repair an existing tutorial using observed evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan verification and maintenance
prompt_templates.prompt: Design verification for [tutorial] and [audience]. Include clean-environment runs, an unaided transfer test, checkpoint CI checks, and measurement priorities. Separate sourced guidelines from adjustable defaults.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: define release checks and ongoing maintenance.

output_examples.input: Plan a webhook tutorial for backend developers who completed our quickstart.
output: Objective: Receive a webhook, verify its signature, and reject a forged event.
Progression: Start a minimal receiver, add signature verification, then require the learner to handle another event type.
Checkpoint: Confirm a valid event succeeds and a forged event fails; document exact outputs after a real run.
Verification: Ask a matching learner to implement an untaught variation without author assistance.

output_examples.input: Two learner runs stopped at signature verification; both also discovered an undocumented tunneling requirement.
output: Priority one: Inspect the verification failure against the published SDK and document the observed output before rewriting.
Hidden prerequisite: Add the tunneling tool to the prerequisites with a version check.
Recovery: Add a troubleshooting entry for the observed error and a resumable checkpoint.
Release check: Repeat the learner run after the failing steps are corrected.

best_practices: Define a testable objective and matching audience before choosing activities or drafting steps.
Use one pinned environment and verify expected outputs through real runs; label anything not yet verified.
Test with representative learners, record step-specific problems, and confirm they can repeat the skill on an untaught variation.
anti_patterns: Add an objective after drafting a feature tour instead of selecting steps that serve a capability.
Provide complete files throughout the tutorial without asking learners to produce the pattern independently.
Treat completion rates, editorial guesses, or self-set thresholds as proof of learning or universal industry standards.

faq.question: How is a tutorial different from a quickstart?
faq.answer: A quickstart proves the product works. A tutorial builds a skill that learners can repeat independently.

faq.question: Can this skill audit an existing tutorial?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses learner-run observations to prioritize step-specific defects, hidden prerequisites, concept gaps, and friction before rewriting.

faq.question: Does it automatically verify every code sample?
faq.answer: No. Verification needs the target environment and real runs. Unverified outputs must be identified and accompanied by a run list.

faq.question: Are its numeric thresholds mandatory standards?
faq.answer: No. It distinguishes sourced guidelines from adjustable defaults, including checkpoint spacing, guidance stages, and verification criteria.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Command verification and persistent context depend on the available tools and environment.

faq.question: Can it support internal engineering onboarding?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers access prerequisites, offline or on-premises command variants, reviewer-visible checkpoints, and verification through the real access process.
